title: Advanced Business Data Structures and Algorithms: Main Exam, 16 December 2019
programme: Bachelor of Business Information Technology / bachelor of Science in Information Technology
unitTitle: Advanced Business Data Structures and Algorithms
instructions: ANSWER QUESTION ONE AND ANY OTHER TWO QUESTIONS. USE ILLUSTRATIONS WHERE NECESSARY.

parts.text: Giving an example in each case, differentiate between linear data structures and non-linear data structures.
Define a stack and state two of its applications. Show how you would check the stack-full and stack-empty conditions.
Using a suitable illustration, define a linked list and state two of its applications.
Describe Prim's minimum spanning tree algorithm.
Explain the difference between dynamic programming and the divide and conquer method.
Define a graph data structure and explain the meaning of the terms topological sorting and graph traversing.
Calculate the maximum number of nodes at level 5 of a binary tree and the maximum number of nodes in a binary tree of depth 3.
How much memory in bytes is required to store two 3-dimensional matrices M(20,10,5) and N(8,15,11), where each element requires 16 bits for storage?
Prove by induction that the sum of k for k = 0 to n equals n(n+1)/2.
Define the term algorithm and distinguish it from the term order of an algorithm.
Describe five features of a good algorithm.
Outline the steps needed in designing and analysing algorithms to perform computational problems.
Explain, giving two examples in each case, the difference between stable sorting and unstable sorting algorithms.
Describe in detail the divide and conquer approach. Explain the pros and cons of this approach.
Describe in detail the merge sort algorithm and the type of problems it is designed to solve.
Use the merge sort algorithm to sort the following data: 4, 1, 8, 2, 10, 6, 9, 3.
Describe in detail the greedy algorithm and its main components.
Discuss two areas of application of the greedy algorithm and state two examples where it fails to find solutions.
Describe the knapsack problem, distinguishing between the 0/1 and fractional versions of the problem.
Write brief notes on the following methods.
Aggregate method
Accounting method
Potential method
Giving relevant examples, distinguish between optimal problems and decision problems.
With the aid of a suitably labelled diagram, describe the n-queens problem and its algorithm.
